name: Dark Folk-Horror Gouache
description: Non-photoreal dark folk-horror illustration: textured gouache and dry-brush scumbling over rough ink wash on visible paper, deep indigo and charcoal shadow, one warm practical light, and a quiet unease carried by the scene rather than by gore.
style_bible: A dark, non-photoreal painted illustration with the texture of gouache worked on paper. Medium and surface: forms are built from opaque gouache and dry-brush scumbling, with rough ink-wash passages carrying the deepest shadow, all sitting on a subtly visible paper surface — so the picture shows its making in every area and never pretends to be a photograph or a clean digital painting. Line: contours stay hand-drawn and irregular, wobbling slightly and varying in weight; they are never clean vectors or uniform strokes. Figures use stylized but believable proportions with expressive, illustrated faces rather than photographic anatomy. Palette: deep indigo and charcoal for the shadow, muted earthy cloth and wood tones for everything the dark does not take, and one restrained warm accent — amber or ochre — supplied by a motivated practical light such as a lamp, a window, a fire or a lantern. No second warm accent, no saturated fill. Value: clear separation between lit and unlit, holding enough midtone detail that silhouettes, hands and faces still read on a phone; the picture must not resolve into a black rectangle. Lighting: every light source is physically grounded in the scene and falls off believably; shadows are cool and deep, never flat. Composition: one strong focal subject set in layered depth with quiet negative space around it. Dread is carried by environmental darkness and a single uneasy visual contradiction inside the scene, never by gore, wounds, monstrosity or threat. Keep the contract content-independent: no fixed nationality, era, creature, recurring prop or copied composition.
